conventions.convention: The standing polyhedral hypotheses are nonempty connectedness (H1), pointwise finite cell incidence (H2), and finitely many cell isometry classes (H3). The global chain distance need not restrict to a cell's Euclidean metric.
Length is the supremum of metric polygonal sums, possibly infinite. Singleton intervals have length zero; arc-length factorization requires a continuous rectifiable path.
Minimizing polyhedral geodesics assume AC. Finite spherical complexes have compact proper complete components without AC; their minimizing-geodesic conclusion assumes AC.
Facet normals point inward. A face link contains unit tangent directions perpendicular to the face direction space; a point link contains all unit inward directions.

Componentwise path distance is auxiliary infinity across components. The angular metric is dπ=min(π,dpath); only dπ enters the cone formula. C(empty) is a point, and joining with the empty link leaves the other factor unchanged.

Large means prescribed simplex edges have length at least π/2, equivalently nonpositive off-diagonal Gram entries. Nonedges receive matrix entry −1. Metric flagness tests pairwise adjacent sets: they span a simplex iff their prescribed cosine matrix is positive definite. The empty matrix is positive definite.
A Coxeter nerve edge exists exactly for finite m and has prescribed cell length π−π/m. This length is distinguished from global chain distance.

The radius-π/2 vertex cap is identified radially as a set and locally isometrically at interior points; an inherited-distance isometry of the entire cap into X is not asserted. Radial insertion stays inside the point-join on the actual isometric link arc.
Girth is the infimum of lengths of isometrically embedded metric circles, with infinity when none exists; CAT(1) comparisons use perimeter strictly below 2π.

load_bearing.statement: Positive-definite diagonal-one Gram matrices realize spherical simplices uniquely up to vertex-preserving linear isometry, with hemisphere and bi-Lipschitz radial coordinates. Compatible finite spherical complexes have compact proper complete length-space components with weak metric topology, and under AC minimizing geodesics. Normal face links have normalized Schur-complement Gram matrices, independent of elimination order; Euclidean face links carry their intrinsic angular metrics.

The angular truncation, Euclidean cone and spherical join formulas define metrics. Dπ-geodesic links give geodesic cones; every minimizing cone geodesic stays within the maximum endpoint radius. The square-sum product of cones is canonically the cone on the spherical join. Under local finiteness and finitely many shapes, a small ball at a relative-interior point of a k-cell is isometric, preserving intrinsic lengths, to the corresponding ball in R^k × C(Lk_X(F)) and in C(Lk_X(p)), with Lk_X(p)≅S^(k−1)*Lk_X(F).

For an isometric polyhedral gluing satisfying (H1)–(H3), chain lengths are independent of measuring cells, all point pairs admit chains, and the chain distance is a metric inducing the weak topology. Every closed bounded subset is compact; the space is proper and complete.

Assume AC. In a finite large metric flag complex that is locally CAT(1) and not CAT(1), the first embedded-circle length m<2π is attained and is the minimum nonshrinkable length. Every length-m minimum nonshrinkable loop is an isometric locally geodesic circle. Genuine vertex-cap excursions have length π; confined constant-length insertion preserves nonshrinkability and old vertex visits. A minimum loop maximizing distinct vertex visits is a locally geodesic edge loop with at most three distinct vertices.

Every face link of a finite large metric flag complex is finite large metric flag. Relative-interior point links are joins of tangent spheres with normal face links, and small spherical neighborhoods have polar cone charts. CAT(1) face links imply local CAT(1); consequently CAT(1) for all smaller-dimensional finite large metric flag complexes implies local CAT(1) in dimension d. Zero-dimensional and empty cases satisfy the truncated CAT(1) tests.

Assume AC. A finite locally CAT(1) large metric flag complex is CAT(1): a short nonshrinkable locally geodesic edge loop would have three edges; their cosine matrix is positive definite, so metric flagness fills the triangle, whose corners strictly shorten and contradict local geodesicity.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every finite large metric flag complex X is CAT(1) for its truncated angular metric dπ.

Under (H1)–(H3), the face order complex gives a compatible barycentric triangulation homeomorphic to X. Global hat coordinates satisfy |λ_v(x)−λ_v(y)|≤L d(x,y) with uniform finite L; some coordinate is at least 1/(D+1), so B(x,1/(2L(D+1))) lies in its open vertex star. Closed stars are finite compact metrizable subcomplexes.

For paths in an arbitrary metric space, length bounds chords and is additive under subdivision; it is lower semicontinuous under uniform convergence. A continuous rectifiable path factors uniquely through its continuous surjective arc-length function into a 1-Lipschitz path whose restriction lengths equal parameter differences. Bounded arc-length families are uniformly equicontinuous.

alerts.finding: F17 says: “With AC, a finite spherical complex with its chain metric is a compact length space with weak metric topology and minimizing geodesics”, citing lem-cg-spherical-simplex-existence-and-link-gram-formula(iii). The opened supplier makes these metric and geodesic assertions componentwise and explicitly assigns auxiliary infinity across distinct components. The universal-Coxeter nerve, allowed by this consumer's hypotheses, has isolated vertices: its chain distance is infinite between them, while its finite truncation has no joining paths and is not a length space. Proof 2.2 also invokes F17 to say the resulting finite spherical chain complex “has a metric whose topology is the weak topology” without specifying componentwise metrics or truncation. Proof 5.1 correctly mentions untruncated component metrics; that later qualification does not make F17 faithful.

seams_checked.note: The companion rank-two example uses the canonical form with off-diagonal −cos(π/m), positivity only on the finite rank-two plane, and the stated determinant, trace and order of the reflection product. It preserves m≥2 and distinguishes the supplementary link length from the acute mirror angle.

Cone equivalence is used with truncated links; compact short-circle and uniqueness-threshold results are applied under AC to compact geodesic untruncated components. The radius and strict perimeter hypotheses are retained.

The nerve definition first obtains the restricted Coxeter system (W_T,T), then applies W_T finite iff its canonical form is positive definite. Empty subsets are handled directly; positivity is not inferred merely from pairwise adjacency.

The minimum-loop proof retains AC, compactness, geodesicity, local CAT(1), normalized loops, and uniform-plus-length short homotopy. It uses attained minima only below 2π. The radial route was also compared with [Davis, Appendix I.7.4, pp. 521–522](https://people.math.osu.edu/davis.12/davisbook.pdf); citation fidelity is assessed against the local supplier's precise shrinkability convention.

The Davis cellulation establishes face-poset and cocycle data, injectivity and intersections, connectedness, finite incidence and finitely many shapes before invoking metric/topology/properness/completeness. The barycentric identification and finite-star uses preserve the supplier conclusions.

The link lemma states AC and proves finite large metric flag links before using the CAT(1) theorem; the Davis CAT(0) theorem retains AC and truncated-link conventions. The alert concerning F17 is a separate citation to the spherical-complex supplier, not a mismatch in this named CAT(1) edge.

The CAT definitions and cone/link theorem retain the cone apex, angular truncation, empty-link convention, normal face links and local product-chart hypotheses. The cone theorem derives the needed geodesic classification locally rather than relying solely on the supplier's existence conclusion.

F12 and Proof 4.1/6.1 use only the choice-free Gram realization and radial homeomorphism clauses: independent unit roots give positive-definite diagonal-one Gram matrices and spherical cone sections. Empty faces are treated separately.
